newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges up, cargoes market cautious.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges up, cargoes market cautious.

text.p: European fuel oil barges rose on Tuesday on a combination of tight supply and slightly increasing demand while cargoes were quiet after a high-priced trade a day earlier kept buyers cautious.

No trades in high sulphur fuel oil barges were heard late in the day after some mid-day deals at $87 a tonne fob Rotterdam, or $1 over Monday's highest deal. A few early morning deals were done at $85.50 and $86 a tonne.
"There is more demand and not that much stuff available," one trader said, adding that by mid-day demand was 15,000 to 20,000 kt compared with all of Monday's 22,000 kt.
But some traders said these prices were manipulated to push the market higher, adding they did not think the current bid/sell range of $86.50/$87 would hold with incoming Russian material.
"There will be M-40 and M-100. At the moment the Russians are asking too much but if they want to sell in the Rotterdam area they will have to lower their prices by $3 or $4," the trader added.
He said the Russians were asking means of the two means plus $2 for M-100. But other traders said no Russian material was being shown at the time being on the NWE barges market.
The high sulphur fuel oil cargo market was reportedly quiet after Monday's trade at $81.75 fob Coryton, which many traders said kept players on the sidelines waiting for the dust to settle.
Sellers were reported to be asking in the $84/$85 range but no buyers were seen, traders said.
One trader said he was in the market on Monday for a parcel of up to 50,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil and was prepared to pay $80/$81 a tonne.
"But when that deal was done at $81.75 I was just blown out of the water," the trader said.
A second trader said: "I don't think any one wants to quote a price for now after that deal."
One percent was said to be a weaker market, with not too many buyers around. But physical prices were a little higher than swaps which traded at lower numbers, $91.50 and $91.75.
One trader said the high freight rates were barring players from concluding deals.
